chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr (he elevated it) from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A servant will be brought on the Day of Judgment having no good deed [in his record], so it will be said to him, 'Remember and recollect, do you have any good deed?' So he will [try to] recall and will say, 'My Lord, I have no good deed except that Your believing servant so-and-so passed by [one day] and asked me for water so that he could perform ablution and pray, so I gave it to him.' So Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, will say, 'Admit My servant into Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: How can a person enter Paradise with no good deeds recorded?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the profound efficacy of *sadaqat* and minor acts of service, such as providing water for ablution, which can serve as a decisive merit for entry into Paradise even when other deeds are absent. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the interconnectedness of the community, where serving a fellow believer is viewed as serving the Imam and, by extension, Allah. The scenario underscores the concept of divine grace (*fadl*) overriding strict accounting, reinforcing the spiritual value of humility and practical kindness in the eschatological judgment.
